title: The Cornell Visit and the Carriers

text.brief: Lee Teng-hui returned to Cornell University on June 9, 1995 to speak at the school where he had earned his doctorate.
text.record: Congress had pressed for his visa by votes of 396 to 0 in the House and 97 to 1 in the Senate. The Party answered with missile tests in the waters off Taiwan in July 1995 and again in March 1996, days before the island's first direct presidential election. Bill Clinton sent two aircraft carrier groups to the area, and Lee won the election.
text.reading: The missile tests beat the grass to startle Taiwan's voters, which is Stratagem 13, and the voters did not startle. The army could not threaten the carriers in 1996, so the Party built the missiles, sensors and submarines that now hold carriers at risk far from the mainland.
text.gapText: Technology Architecture. American power in the strait rested on platforms whose freedom of action the adversary could study and erode.
text.fix: Plan the next crisis against the forces the adversary built after the last one.
